Bivar Capital — Quantitative Research

UK Optimal MomentumSystematic momentum with cash regime overlay

A long-only momentum strategy on UK (LSE) equities with a profitability filter, market regime overlay, and a cash allocation during bear markets. Net of UK stamp duty (0.5% SDRT) and slippage. 302 months of out-of-sample backtesting with monthly data. Signal at month-end, execution on the first trading day of the next month. No look-ahead bias.

Revised 2026-08-16. This report replaces an earlier version that ran a different, non-canonical configuration (top 7, pure 6-month momentum, >£250M mcap, no transaction costs). This version matches extensive sensitivity testing across portfolio size, regime window, market cap threshold, momentum formula, and fundamental filters — see Sections XI–XIII — and is net of realistic UK trading costs.

I. Strategy Specification

Signal: End of each month

  1. Regime check: Is the FTSE 100 close above its 200-day simple moving average?
    • NO → Sell all stocks. Move to cash. Hold until next month’s signal.
    • YES → Proceed to step 2.
  2. Compute momentum for every eligible stock:
    Momentum = 50% × (price / price 6 months ago − 1) + 50% × (price / price 9 months ago − 1)
  3. Filter universe:
    • Market capitalisation > £100 million
    • EBIT (TTM) > 0 (operating profit positive, most recent report)
    • LSE common stock, GBX-denominated only
  4. Select top 7 by momentum composite. Equal weight (~14.3% each).
  5. Execute on the 1st trading day of the next month: sell positions that left the portfolio, buy new ones. Costs: 0.79% on buys (0.50% stamp duty + 0.29% spread), 0.29% on sells.
Why momentum works: Stocks that have risen tend to continue rising. Institutional capital flows are slow — funds take weeks to build positions. Information propagates gradually. Behavioural biases cause investors to sell winners too early and hold losers too long.
Why cash during bear markets: The MA200 regime filter identifies bear markets early — switching to cash avoids the stock drawdown entirely instead of trying to time a hedge. Simpler and more robust than holding a second asset (gold, bonds, etc.) that introduces its own data source, its own risk, and its own failure modes.

X. Why Each Parameter

Momentum blend: 50% × 6-month + 50% × 9-month

Tested against pure 3m/6m/9m/12m and multiple weighted blends (Section XI). This combination delivered the highest Sharpe ratio and sits inside a coherent region (6–12 months) rather than an isolated spike — both shorter (3M) and longer (15–24M) lookbacks degrade sharply and monotonically, consistent with the standard momentum literature.

Market cap > £100M

Tested against £150M/£200M/£250M/£350M/£500M thresholds at multiple N and MA combinations (Section XII sensitivity work). £100M consistently gave the best Sharpe and MaxDD at every N/MA combination tested — a smooth, monotonic gradient, not an isolated best cell.

EBIT > 0

The single most important fundamental filter. Removing it collapses Sharpe from 0.99 to 0.53 and roughly doubles drawdown. Stricter alternatives (net income positive, EBIT margin thresholds, revenue/EBIT growth, positive free cash flow) were all tested and all underperform plain EBIT>0 — they shrink the eligible universe and cut out exactly the early-stage/turnaround names that produce the strongest momentum.

MA200 regime filter

When the FTSE 100 closes below its 200-day moving average, the strategy exits all stock positions and moves to cash. Without this filter, maximum drawdown reaches -48%. With it, drawdown is contained to -35.0%.

Cash during bear months

Cash during bear months avoids the stock drawdown outright, with no second asset, no extra data source, and no additional failure mode to audit.

Transaction costs: 0.79% buy / 0.29% sell

UK shares carry a 0.5% Stamp Duty Reserve Tax (SDRT) on purchases (not sales), plus 0.29% per leg (58.2bps round-trip, IBKR real median spread, measured 2026-08-18) for small/mid-cap UK names. At ~44% average monthly turnover (roughly 3 of 7 positions replaced every month), this costs approximately 4.5 percentage points of CAGR versus the gross backtest.

Key takeaway: The MA200 regime filter and the EBIT>0 filter are both doing real, independent work — removing either one materially worsens Sharpe and drawdown. This ablation's "FULL" row is the exact same configuration as the main backtest above.

EBIT vs Net Income: average eligible universe (mcap>£100M + profitability test passed, before momentum ranking) is 395 names/month under EBIT>0 vs 332 names/month under NetIncome>0 — Net Income is a stricter screen here, since it also nets out interest expense and tax, which EBIT ignores.

Data-quality fix applied (2026-08-19). Five tickers — Mindflair (MFAI), Biome Technologies (BIOM), Norman Broadbent (NBB), IGas Energy (IGAS), Vela Technologies (VELA) — were confirmed via forensic audit to carry corrupted EODHD price data: MFAI/NBB/IGAS/VELA alternate between a real traded price and the literal 999999.9999 EODHD sentinel error value (producing fake repeating ~−97% "crashes"); BIOM shows isolated single-day bad ticks on near-zero volume. No corporate action (split, rights issue) explains any of these moves in either ticker's records. All five are now excluded from the entire backtest universe at the data-loading stage (not just this table) — every number in this report, including the Performance Summary, reflects the cleaned data.

XIV. Look-Ahead Bias Audit

Signal & Execution Timeline

Month-end (signal): Compute momentum using historical month-end prices (6 and 9 months back). Check FTSE 100 vs its 200-day moving average. All data is from the past. ✓

1st trading day of next month (execution): Buy/sell using next-month price data. No same-month execution. ✓

Data Sources Verified

DataSourceTimingStatus
Stock prices (momentum)EODHD adjusted closeSignal month-end and 6/9 months prior✓ Past only
FTSE 100 (MA200)Yahoo FinanceSignal date close vs last 200 days✓ Past only
Market capEODHD outstandingShares × pricePoint-in-time annual shares✓ Past only
EBIT (TTM)EODHD quarterly, via filing_datePoint-in-time avail_date, ~60 day fallback lag✓ Past only
Execution pricesEODHD adjusted closeNext month, after signal✓ No same-month
Conclusion: No look-ahead bias detected. Signal uses only past prices. Fundamentals use point-in-time filing dates, not period-end dates.

XV. Risks & Caveats

  • Transaction costs included (0.79%/0.29% buy/sell, ≈108bps round-trip) — unlike some earlier versions of this report. ~44% average monthly turnover costs ~4.5pp of CAGR versus gross.
  • Overfitting risk. N, MA window, mcap threshold and momentum formula were all swept independently; the chosen config sits inside smooth, monotonic regions rather than isolated spikes on every dimension tested, which is reassuring but not proof against overfit.
  • ~25 years, multiple bear markets. Includes the dot-com bust, 2008 GFC, and 2020 COVID crash.
  • Concentration risk. 7 stocks at 14.3% each. A single-stock blowup costs ~14% of the portfolio.
  • Small/mid-cap liquidity. £100M mcap floor reaches into genuinely small, less liquid UK names; the 0.29%/leg spread assumption (real median, but a single point-in-time snapshot) may be optimistic in size or in stressed markets.

XVI. Real Spread & Liquidity Robustness

Trading costs throughout this report: 0.50% UK stamp duty (SDRT, buy-side) + 0.58% average bid/ask spread (IBKR, real median across the strategy's historical holdings, measured 2026-08-18) ≈ 108bps round-trip.

Real spread measurement. On 2026-08-18, real bid/ask spreads were pulled via IBKR (delayed data) for the full historical universe of names this strategy has ever selected since 2001 (318 unique tickers). 216 returned a valid live quote (68% coverage) — the rest have since been delisted, renamed, or acquired and have no resolvable contract today. Distribution across the 216 covered names: median 58.2bps, mean 68.4bps (excluding one clear outlier, Filtronic/FTC at 392bps), IQR [25.3, 105.9]bps. This is a single point-in-time snapshot used as a static proxy for each ticker's liquidity at every historical month it was held — an approximation, not true point-in-time historical spread data (which isn't obtainable).

Liquidity-filter sensitivity (exploratory, N=10 — not the live N=7 configuration)

Same 50%×6M+50%×9M / >£100M / EBIT>0 / MA200 selection, with an additional real-spread eligibility screen applied before ranking, shown here purely as a reference point for how sensitive the strategy is to execution cost discipline.

VariantGross CAGR/Sharpe/MaxDD Net — flat 170bpsNet — real spread + 50bps stamp
No filter23.1% / 1.19 / −24.4%17.5% / 0.95 / −28.0%15.0% / 0.83 / −32.9%
Liquid ≤30bps19.9% / 1.23 / −26.0%15.5% / 1.01 / −32.1%18.2% / 1.15 / −28.4%
Liquid ≤50bps21.0% / 1.28 / −23.4%16.5% / 1.05 / −27.4%19.2% / 1.19 / −25.1%

No live parameter change was made as a result of this analysis. The strategy running in uk_momentum_signal.py remains N=7 stocks, £100M market-cap floor, unchanged. A separate test raised the mcap floor to £800M using real point-in-time historical market cap (not the spread proxy) and performed materially worse — 13.5% vs 25.2% gross CAGR — so no floor increase was adopted either. Instead, the user reviews the real bid/ask spread manually before executing each trade and skips names that look too wide, as an informal execution safeguard rather than a coded filter.
